title: Function machines and inverse operations
learning_objectives: Use a function machine to represent an operation and its inverse; solve one-step equations by undoing
key_content: Inverse operations; one-step equations x + 5 = 12, 3x = 21; reading algebraic notation
teaching_approach: Function machines drawn for every example; pupils build the forward machine then reverse it

title: Two-step equations with the balance
learning_objectives: Solve two-step equations by doing the same to both sides; represent an equation as a bar model
key_content: Two-step equations 3x + 4 = 19, 2x − 5 = 9; balance method; bar model
teaching_approach: Balance method throughout: every step written as 'do the same to both sides'. Bar model drawn before symbols for the first three examples
resources: Balance scales (physical) for the demo; bar model worksheet

title: Collecting like terms
learning_objectives: Simplify expressions by collecting like terms, including negatives
teaching_approach: Algebra tiles on the visualiser; sort terms by colour before combining

title: Unknowns on both sides
learning_objectives: Solve equations with the unknown on both sides using the balance method; explain why the sign changes
key_content: 5x + 3 = 2x + 12; subtracting the smaller x-term from both sides; common mistake: moving a term without changing its sign
teaching_approach: Balance and bar model. Explicit 'common mistake' slot: pupils find the error in a worked solution. We do NOT teach 'change side, change sign'
resources: Worksheet 'Common mistake: why the sign changes'; homework 'Mixed practice: both sides'

title: Expanding single brackets and equations with brackets
learning_objectives: Expand a single bracket using the grid method; solve equations with brackets by expanding first then balancing
key_content: Expand 3(x + 2), −2(x − 3) with negatives; solve 3(x + 2) = 21; expand then balance
teaching_approach: Grid method for every expansion; then the balance method as in week 4. Negative numbers revisited as a starter

title: Linear inequalities
learning_objectives: Solve linear inequalities and represent solutions on a number line
key_content: Inequality symbols; solving as for equations; number line with open and closed circles
teaching_approach: Balance method carried over; number line drawn for every answer

title: Forming equations from words
learning_objectives: Form and solve a linear equation from a worded problem or a perimeter problem
key_content: Translate a sentence or a diagram into an equation; solve with the balance method
teaching_approach: Bar model to represent the problem before writing the equation
